name: Copilot CLI Trace Viewer
description: Render Copilot CLI OpenTelemetry JSONL into a Job Summary, self-contained HTML viewer, and canonical SPA data.
inputs:
  trace-path:
    description: Path to the Copilot CLI OpenTelemetry JSONL file.
    required: true
  html-path:
    description: Destination path for the self-contained HTML viewer.
    required: true
  data-path:
    description: Optional destination for the canonical machine-readable trace model used by the online SPA.
    default: ""
  include-messages:
    description: Include redacted request/response payloads with safe hydration of runner-temp tool output.
    default: "false"
  require-model:
    description: Comma-separated models that must be observed; every model call must use one of them.
    default: ""
  require-pattern-evidence:
    description: Orchestration pattern ID whose expected trace topology must be observed; false disables validation.
    default: "false"
  pricing-path:
    description: Optional path to a model-keyed pricing JSON file; defaults to the bundled GitHub Copilot catalog.
    default: ""
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Render trace
      shell: bash
      env:
        TRACE_HTML_PATH: ${{ inputs.html-path }}
        TRACE_DATA_PATH: ${{ inputs.data-path }}
        TRACE_INCLUDE_MESSAGES: ${{ inputs.include-messages }}
        REQUIRE_MODEL: ${{ inputs.require-model }}
        REQUIRE_PATTERN_EVIDENCE: ${{ inputs.require-pattern-evidence }}
        TRACE_PATTERN: ${{ inputs.require-pattern-evidence }}
        PRICING_PATH: ${{ inputs.pricing-path }}
      run: node "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/render-trace.mjs" "${{ inputs.trace-path }}"

name: Publish Copilot Trace Viewers

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Copilot CLI Agent Demos"]
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: write
  pages: write

concurrency:
  group: copilot-trace-pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == github.event.repository.default_branch
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Check out publisher
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          path: source
      - name: Download trace artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: copilot-trace-viewer
          path: report
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
      - name: Check out Pages
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: gh-pages
          path: pages
      - name: Publish trace data
        env:
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          RUN_TITLE: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.display_title }}
          RUN_CREATED_AT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.created_at }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
        run: node source/.github/scripts/publish-trace-pages.mjs report pages source
      - name: Push Pages update
        working-directory: pages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add .
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Trace Viewer Pages site is already current."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "Publish trace viewer for run ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}"
          git push origin HEAD:gh-pages
          gh api --method POST "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pages/builds" >/dev/null

events.response:
# ai-native-sdlc

Manually run **Copilot CLI Agent Demos** from Actions. Open the completed run's **Job Summary** to see the observed parent/subagent/model/tool hierarchy, timestamps, durations, parallel-agent peak, token counts, and cost. Each successful run uploads a **copilot-trace-viewer** artifact containing the offline HTML report and canonical trace data. A separate publisher consumes that artifact and stores only the redacted canonical JSON on GitHub Pages. The shared **Copilot CLI Trace Viewer** SPA loads `/traces/<run-id>.json`, so one renderer serves every historical run and UI improvements apply without regenerating old reports. The viewer provides **Trace** and **Dependencies** tabs, correlated selection, filtering, model-aware cost, and SVG/PNG graph export.

Repository collaborators can choose one of four **Copilot CLI demo** issue forms. Each form represents exactly one orchestration pattern, exposes one editable task, and carries an internal `copilot-pattern:*` routing label instead of showing a redundant pattern dropdown. Creating or reopening the resulting `copilot-agent-demo` issue starts the shared workflow. Both model selectors remain available, and detailed tracing with redacted request/response payloads is selected by default. When the run finishes, the workflow posts the final result, trace diagnostics, dependency graph, workflow link, one-click online Trace Viewer link, and downloadable offline HTML artifact back to the originating issue.

Issue comments always include a GitHub-rendered Mermaid dependency graph. To additionally embed the generated PNG as a GitHub user attachment, configure the optional `AGENT_TRACE_MEDIA_TOKEN` Actions secret with a user token that can access this repository. GitHub's short-lived Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not accepted by the user-attachments upload endpoint and returns 404; the workflow therefore never uses it for media upload and safely falls back to Mermaid if the optional upload is unavailable.

The issue form and manual dispatch support four reusable orchestration patterns:

- **Direct execution** handles the task without delegation, providing a cost and latency baseline.
- **Parallel delegation** fans out independent subtasks or perspectives and synthesizes their results.
- **Critic-reviser loop** challenges an initial position before producing a revised conclusion.
- **Sequential pipeline** passes one subagent's result into the next stage before final synthesis.

The repository stores only these stable orchestration patterns. Each issue supplies an editable task, so every issue can become a new demo without adding implementation files or changing the workflow. Copilot CLI decides the concrete subagent type at runtime.

Every reusable pattern includes a generic tested fallback task and an internal orchestration contract. Issue forms provide their editable demonstration scenarios independently, without coupling scenario content to the reusable pattern implementation.

See [Copilot CLI agent orchestration patterns](docs/copilot-cli-agent-orchestration-patterns.md) for execution diagrams, model behavior, validation signals, failure interpretation, and guidance on choosing a pattern.

The dependency-free implementation in `trace-viewer/` is also a local composite action. `trace-model.mjs` normalizes direct CLI JSONL and OTLP envelopes into one trace view model; `html-renderer.mjs` renders that model; `render-trace.mjs` is the action/CLI adapter. The demo calls it with `uses: ./trace-viewer`; other workflows can pass an OTEL JSONL `trace-path`, a stable `html-path`, optional model/evidence/message requirements, and an optional replacement pricing catalog.

The workflow exposes **Orchestrator model** and **Subagent model** choices, both defaulting to `gpt-6-luna`. The orchestrator delegates work and synthesizes the final response; dynamically created subagents are instructed to use the selected subagent model. Parallel demos use `--fleet`; sequential demos let the orchestrator create each subagent only after the previous result returns. OTEL trace evidence validates branch counts, concurrency/order, tool use, and observed models without depending on predetermined agent names. The repository owner's Copilot entitlement must include the selected models.

The workflow runs from `workflow_dispatch` or an authorized `copilot-agent-demo` issue, installs Node 22 and `@github/copilot`, and authenticates Copilot with the run's short-lived `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: read`, `copilot-requests: write`). The repository owner needs a Copilot entitlement and available usage; usage in a personal repository is billed to that owner's Copilot seat. Organization repositories additionally need the Copilot CLI organization billing policy. The optional user-attachment upload uses the separate `AGENT_TRACE_MEDIA_TOKEN` secret described above.

The checked-in `.github/mcp.json` allows only two read-only tools on the public, unauthenticated [Microsoft Learn MCP server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/support/mcp); the headless workflow opts in to loading this workspace MCP configuration. External URLs are not preapproved by the generic workflow. Because the Parallel delegation form's default scenario compares AWS and Azure, that form preselects only `docs.aws.amazon.com`; its validated selection is passed to Copilot CLI as `--allow-url`, while Azure research uses Microsoft Learn MCP. Users should select **Block all external URLs** when replacing the task with one that does not need AWS documentation.

CLI OpenTelemetry writes JSONL to the runner's temporary directory; **redacted request/response capture is on by default** and the raw trace is never uploaded. Select **Metadata only** in an issue form or disable **include_messages** during manual dispatch when payloads should not appear in the artifact. Copilot CLI may replace a large tool result with a runner-temp file reference. Before the runner is destroyed, the trace model safely resolves only Copilot tool-output files under the runner temp directory, redacts their contents, and embeds the result in the report. Payloads are preserved up to a 1 MiB safety ceiling instead of being arbitrarily clipped at 1,200 characters. Absolute runner paths are not published. Redaction is best-effort, so use metadata-only mode on private prompts, sensitive repositories, or sessions with secrets.

Cost uses `gen_ai.usage.cost` when OTEL reports it. Otherwise the renderer normalizes each span's model name, looks it up in `trace-viewer/model-pricing.json`, selects its default or long-context tier, and estimates the call from observed input/output/cache token counts. The viewer shows the trace total, each model call, and root-inspector rollups by agent branch and model, including priced-call coverage and token totals. The bundled catalog covers the current OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, xAI, and Moonshot models listed on GitHub's [models and pricing](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing) page. A workflow can pass `pricing-path` to replace the bundled catalog. Unknown models or calls without token usage display `—` and are excluded from the total rather than receiving another model's rate.

The renderer accepts both direct CLI span records and OTLP `resourceSpans[].scopeSpans[].spans[]`. A missing or malformed trace fails visibly (even if Copilot fails). Treat GitHub Pages reports, artifacts, and the Job Summary as public in this repository. The Pages publisher reads the artifact with its workflow token, validates the canonical schema, and publishes only `trace-data.json`; it never publishes the raw OTEL JSONL. The browser never receives a GitHub token and does not fetch Actions artifacts directly.

GitHub Pages is configured to deploy from the root of the `gh-pages` branch. The publisher serializes branch updates so concurrent demo runs cannot overwrite one another; each run keeps an immutable `/traces/<run-id>.json` URL while the shared `/viewer/` application is refreshed from the renderer version used by the newest published run.

OpenTelemetry span status `UNSET` (`code: 0`) does not mean that the outcome is unknown. The renderer treats a span as successful unless OTEL reports `ERROR` (`code: 2`) or an error attribute, which prevents healthy auto-instrumented tool calls from being labeled `unknown`.

Failed spans show the OTEL failure reason in the inspector even when message capture is disabled. A fast failed tool call can be an intentional permission-policy rejection—for example, an external `web_fetch` call is rejected when its URL was not preapproved, while configured MCP tools remain available.

Run the local, dependency-free parser tests with `node --test trace-viewer/render-trace.test.mjs`.

References: [CLI in Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli-in-actions), [CLI tool permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/allowing-tools), [workspace MCP configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers), [Learn MCP tools](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/support/mcp-developer-reference), [Actions billing](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

name: Copilot CLI Agent Demos

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pattern:
        description: "Orchestration pattern to demonstrate"
        type: choice
        default: Parallel delegation
        options:
          - Direct execution
          - Parallel delegation
          - Critic-reviser loop
          - Sequential pipeline
      orchestrator_model:
        description: "Model that delegates to subagents and synthesizes the final result"
        type: choice
        default: gpt-6-luna
        options:
          - gpt-6-luna
          - gpt-6-sol
          - gpt-6-astra
          - gpt-5.6-luna
          - gpt-5.6-terra
          - gpt-5.6-sol
          - gpt-5.5
          - gpt-5.4
          - gpt-5.4-mini
          - gpt-5.3-codex
          - gpt-5-mini
          - claude-sonnet-5
          - claude-sonnet-4.6
          - gemini-3.8-flash
          - grok-4.7
          - mai-code-1.1-flash
      subagent_model:
        description: "Model shared by the specialist agents"
        type: choice
        default: gpt-6-luna
        options:
          - gpt-6-luna
          - gpt-6-sol
          - gpt-6-astra
          - gpt-5.6-luna
          - gpt-5.6-terra
          - gpt-5.6-sol
          - gpt-5.5
          - gpt-5.4
          - gpt-5.4-mini
          - gpt-5.3-codex
          - gpt-5-mini
          - claude-sonnet-5
          - claude-sonnet-4.6
          - gemini-3.8-flash
          - grok-4.7
          - mai-code-1.1-flash
      include_messages:
        description: "Include redacted request/response payloads in the public Pages report and HTML artifact"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      task_prompt:
        description: "Concrete task for this demo; leave empty to use a generic repository task"
        type: string
        required: false
      agent_instructions:
        description: "Optional guidance for how Copilot should divide the task among dynamic subagents"
        type: string
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  copilot-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: copilot-agent-demo-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  demo:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (
        contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'copilot-agent-demo') &&
        contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.issue.author_association)
      )
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      COPILOT_OTEL_ENABLED: "true"
      COPILOT_OTEL_EXPORTER_TYPE: file
      OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT: "false"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Install Copilot CLI
        run: npm install -g @github/copilot
      - name: Prepare demo request
        id: request
        env:
          INPUT_ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL: ${{ inputs.orchestrator_model }}
          INPUT_SUBAGENT_MODEL: ${{ inputs.subagent_model }}
          INPUT_INCLUDE_MESSAGES: ${{ inputs.include_messages }}
          INPUT_PATTERN: ${{ inputs.pattern }}
          INPUT_TASK_PROMPT: ${{ inputs.task_prompt }}
          INPUT_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS: ${{ inputs.agent_instructions }}
          TRACE_PROMPT_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-demo-prompt.txt
          TRACE_INSTRUCTION_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-demo-instruction.txt
        run: node .github/scripts/prepare-demo-request.mjs
      - name: Run orchestrated read-only analysis
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL: ${{ steps.request.outputs.orchestrator_model }}
          TRACE_PROMPT_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-demo-prompt.txt
          TRACE_INSTRUCTION_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-demo-instruction.txt
          EXECUTION_MODE: ${{ steps.request.outputs.execution }}
          ALLOWED_URL: ${{ steps.request.outputs.allowed_url }}
          GITHUB_COPILOT_PROMPT_MODE_WORKSPACE_MCP: "true"
          OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT: ${{ steps.request.outputs.include_messages }}
          COPILOT_OTEL_FILE_EXPORTER_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-otel.jsonl
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          mkdir -p trace-report
          REQUEST="$(cat "$TRACE_PROMPT_PATH")"
          INSTRUCTION="$(cat "$TRACE_INSTRUCTION_PATH")"
          EXTRA_ARGS=()
          if [ "$EXECUTION_MODE" = "fleet" ]; then
            EXTRA_ARGS+=(--fleet)
          fi
          if [ -n "$ALLOWED_URL" ]; then
            EXTRA_ARGS+=(--allow-url="$ALLOWED_URL")
          else
            EXTRA_ARGS+=(--available-tools='view,glob,rg,task,read_agent,list_agents,sql,microsoft-learn')
          fi
          copilot --model "$ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL" -p "$INSTRUCTION

          Task:
          $REQUEST" \
            "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}" \
            --allow-tool='web_fetch,microsoft-learn' \
            --deny-tool=write --deny-tool=shell | tee trace-report/copilot-response.md
      - name: Render trace viewer
        if: always()
        uses: ./trace-viewer
        with:
          trace-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/copilot-otel.jsonl
          html-path: ${{ github.workspace }}/trace-report/copilot-trace-report.html
          data-path: ${{ github.workspace }}/trace-report/trace-data.json
          include-messages: ${{ steps.request.outputs.include_messages }}
          require-model: ${{ steps.request.outputs.required_models }}
          require-pattern-evidence: ${{ steps.request.outputs.pattern }}
      - name: Capture dependency map
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ ! -f trace-report/copilot-trace-report.html ]; then
            echo "HTML trace report is unavailable; skipping dependency-map capture." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          node trace-viewer/capture-dependency-map.mjs \
            trace-report/copilot-trace-report.html \
            trace-report/dependency-map.png
      - name: Attach HTML trace viewer
        if: always()
        id: trace_artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: copilot-trace-viewer
          path: trace-report/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Publish dependency image
        id: media
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'issues'
        env:
          MEDIA_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AGENT_TRACE_MEDIA_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$MEDIA_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::notice::AGENT_TRACE_MEDIA_TOKEN is not configured; the issue comment will use a Mermaid dependency graph."
            exit 0
          fi
          FILE='trace-report/dependency-map.png'
          NAME="$(basename -- "$FILE")"
          MIME='image/png'
          REPO='${{ github.repository }}'
          if [ ! -f "$FILE" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Dependency-map image is unavailable; the issue comment will use Mermaid."
            exit 0
          fi
          REPO_ID="$(GH_TOKEN="$MEDIA_TOKEN" gh api "repos/$REPO" --jq .id)" || {
            echo "::warning::Repository lookup for the dependency image failed; the issue comment will use Mermaid."
            exit 0
          }
          case "$REPO_ID" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::warning::Repository ID is invalid; the issue comment will use Mermaid."
              exit 0
              ;;
          esac
          RESPONSE_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/dependency-image-upload.json"
          if ! curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST \
            'https://uploads.github.com/user-attachments/assets' \
            --url-query "name=$NAME" \
            --url-query "content_type=$MIME" \
            --url-query "repository_id=$REPO_ID" \
            -H 'Accept: application/json' \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
            -H 'X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28' \
            -H "Authorization: [REDACTED] \
            --data-binary "@$FILE" > "$RESPONSE_PATH"; then
            echo "::warning::GitHub rejected the dependency image upload; the issue comment will use Mermaid."
            exit 0
          fi
          URL="$(jq -r '.url // empty' "$RESPONSE_PATH")"
          case "$URL" in
            https://*) echo "url=$URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;;
            *) echo "::warning::GitHub returned no dependency image URL; the issue comment will use Mermaid." ;;
          esac
      - name: Post result to issue
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'issues'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL: ${{ steps.request.outputs.orchestrator_model || 'unavailable' }}
          SUBAGENT_MODEL: ${{ steps.request.outputs.subagent_model || 'unavailable' }}
